incident.description: Customers lose their carts mid checkout. A checkout deploy went out around the same time.

scenario: Harmless deploy close in time to the real cause

finding.summary: Investigation of logs and metrics for checkout and cart services from 11:00 to 11:20 revealed error logs in checkout due to missing cart sessions in cache, along with an elevated error rate in us-east. No cart service logs or metrics were recorded in this period.

claims.text: At 2026-03-12T11:03, checkout service logged an ERROR: "cart session not found in cache session=c20d".
The checkout service error_rate metric in us-east recorded values of 0.12, 0.13, and 0.13 at 5-minute intervals starting at 2026-03-12T11:00.
Checkout error rates coincided with session cache lookup failures during the 11:00 to 11:20 window.

gaps: No log lines or metric series were found for the cart service during the 11:00 to 11:20 window.

claims.text: At 2026-03-12T11:00, service checkout underwent deployment dep-01 (version v5.1.2: update footer copy).
Checkout service downstream/upstream dependencies include gateway (downstream), payments, inventory, auth, and redis (upstreams).
No other deployments or configuration changes were found for checkout, cart, or upstream services between 2026-03-12T08:00 and 2026-03-12T11:20.

assumptions: The deployment v5.1.2 introduced a bug causing cache keys to be misformatted or session lookups to fail

finding.summary: Between 11:00 and 11:20 on 2026-03-12, the redis service in us-east showed 100% memory utilization and high key eviction rates (9,100–9,300 evictions/min), up from 0 evictions prior to 10:55. No redis log entries were found during this window.

claims.text: No log entries were found for the redis service between 11:00 and 11:20 on 2026-03-12.
The redis service in us-east reached 100% memory utilization (1.0) starting at 10:55 and remained at 1.0 from 11:00 to 11:10 on 2026-03-12.
The evicted_keys_per_min metric for redis in us-east was 0 until 10:50, then spiked to 8,400 at 10:55 and stayed elevated between 9,100 and 9,300 evictions per minute from 11:00 to 11:10.
The redis cache in us-east experienced severe memory pressure resulting in high rates of key evictions between 11:00 and 11:20 on 2026-03-12.

hypotheses.statement: Redis cache memory exhaustion in us-east caused high key eviction rates starting at 10:55, purging active cart session data and causing checkouts to fail with missing sessions.
assumptions: Cart session data was stored in the shared Redis cache without eviction protection or persistence, causing cart keys to be evicted when Redis hit 100% memory utilization.

hypotheses.statement: Checkout deployment dep-01 (v5.1.2) at 11:00 caused cart sessions to be dropped or misread by the checkout service.
assumptions: The v5.1.2 deploy introduced an undocumented regression or side effect that affected cache reads or cleared cart sessions upon deployment.

hypotheses.statement: A traffic surge or sudden increase in session creation led to Redis memory saturation and key evictions.
assumptions: An unexpected increase in cart creations or session volume filled Redis memory to capacity prior to 10:55.

report.summary: The investigation into carts emptying during checkout is inconclusive. The hypotheses evaluated (Redis session key evictions due to memory saturation/exhaustion vs checkout deployment v5.1.2 dropping/misreading session data) all have low confidence with no clear leading cause. Missing evidence includes cart service logs/metrics during the 11:00-11:20 window, feature flag configuration history, and cart service dependency mappings.
